title: The top of the payroll: the 100 highest-paid people, year by year
question: How much were the 100 highest-paid City employees paid each fiscal year, how much of it was salary, overtime and other pay, and how did it move against the pay of the middle employee?
finding: The 100 highest-paid people averaged $277,570 in fiscal 2013 and $562,109 in fiscal 2026, a rise of 103%; the middle person on the payroll went from $72,135 to $127,713, a rise of 77%. Stopping at fiscal 2025, the last year of ordinary length, the rises are 82% and 61%. The top 100 were paid 3.8 times the middle person in fiscal 2013 and 4.4 times in fiscal 2026. What changed is overtime: it was 17% of the top 100’s pay in fiscal 2013 and 44% in fiscal 2026, while regular salary fell from 66% to 46% of it. It took $489,350 to be in the top 100 in fiscal 2026, against $245,674 in fiscal 2013.
how: City payroll file, fiscal 2013 to 2026. Pay is salary, overtime and other pay; benefits are left out. Board and commission seats and the Superior Court are left out. Before fiscal 2017 the file carries a number for each person and the rows under one number are added together; from fiscal 2017 it carries names, and two rows are added together only when the name is rare enough to follow, the department is the same and the hours fit one person. Otherwise each row counts separately, so two people who share a name are never merged. The middle employee is the middle value of everyone paid anything in the year, part-year and part-time staff included, because hours are on file only from fiscal 2017; the “full year” column is the middle of those with full-time hours. In this file a full-time year is 2,080 paid hours in every fiscal year from 2017 to 2025 and 2,160 in fiscal 2026 (27 fortnights of 80 hours rather than 26), so every yearly amount for fiscal 2026 is about 3.8% larger than a like-for-like year.
limits: High pay is not misconduct. A single year at the top can be back pay, a settlement or a payout of unused leave, which is money already earned. Someone who changed department in a year appears as two rows and can be undercounted. The middle employee includes part-timers, whose numbers change from year to year. Overtime beyond what one person could plausibly work is examined in the overtime pages, not here.

sources.t: San Francisco Controller: Employee Compensation, fiscal 2013 to 2026 (DataSF)
